sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 3.3% a year from $65.1 billion in FY2017 to $87.0 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F201].
The path was not smooth: FY2019 operating income fell 58.9% to $5.5 billion on an 8.1% operating margin, then FY2020 rebounded 186.2% to $15.7 billion [F13][F23][F14][D97][D148].

The FY2019 trough was an $8.3 billion impairment charge, including $6.8 billion of Shave Care goodwill, driven by currency devaluations, decelerating grooming category growth and tougher US competition [X112][X109][P62].

FY2020's rebound reflected $8.3 billion of that base-period charge plus the net sales increase and gross margin gain, with volume lifted by COVID-19 demand for cleaning and health products [P71][P72].
Since FY2020 growth has been steady but slower, with revenue up 2.0% a year over FY2023 to FY2026 [D664].
The US was the growth engine for most of the window, contributing +2.2pp of FY2024 revenue growth and +1.3pp in FY2025, before fading to +0.1pp in FY2026 [D530][D533][D536].
In FY2026 the mix reversed: Non-US contributed +3.1pp of the 3.3% revenue growth while the US added just +0.1pp [D511][D457][D536].
FY2026 net sales rose 3% on favorable foreign exchange of 2% and pricing of 1%, with unit volume and mix unchanged [P26].
Fabric & Home Care is the largest segment at 34.8% of revenue and contributed +0.8pp in FY2026, while Beauty added +1.3pp on 7.1% growth [D541][D543][D603][D602].
Operating income grew faster than revenue over the window, at a 4.1% CAGR against 3.3%, but fell 3.4% in FY2026 as costs outgrew sales by 2.1pp [F202][F201][D458][D482].
FY2026 operating margin of 22.7% sits just above the 22.1% window median but below the 24.3% FY2025 high, and far above the 8.1% FY2019 low [F30][D648][D647][D646].
The 1.6pp FY2026 decline came from a lower gross margin and higher marketing spending, with cost of revenue costing 1.0pp and SG&A 0.6pp [D470][P25][D483][D485].
Gross margin fell on unfavorable category mix, partly offset by lower commodity costs and productivity savings [P5].
Net margin of 18.4% matched its window median despite the operating decline, helped by other income of $1.1 billion versus $154 million in FY2025 [F50][D651][X108][X107].
That swing reflected the prior-year Argentina translation charge and the current-year Glad joint venture dissolution gain [P24].
Operating cash flow of $19.6 billion was 1.22x net income in FY2026, and free cash flow of $15.1 billion was 0.94x, below the 1.02x window median for that ratio [F80][F40][D444][F100][D445][D660].
Free cash flow margin of 17.4% is close to the 17.2% window median and well above the 9.2% staples peer median [D441][D654][D673].
Operating cash flow rose 10% as net earnings plus non-cash items generated about $19.5 billion, with inventory consuming $641 million and payables generating $919 million [P3].
Capex rose 16.9% to $4.4 billion, 5.1% of revenue and 1.40x D&A, the highest capital intensity in the window [F90][D464][D440][D446].
Net debt was $24.2 billion, or 27.8% of revenue, against a staples peer median of -1.0% net cash, placing it in the 33rd percentile of six peers [D450][D451][D677][D676].
Long-term debt fell 8.6% to $22.8 billion while cash rose 4.0% to $9.9 billion, and the current ratio of 0.68x is below the 0.72x window median [F190][D468][F140][D466][F180][D663].
Buybacks of $5.0 billion plus dividends of $10.2 billion were 100.7% of free cash flow in FY2026, down from 116.6% in FY2025 [X134][X144][D453][D402].
The diluted share count fell 1.3% to 2,422.5 million, so EPS grew 1.7% while net income grew 0.5% [X124][D476][D461][D459].

The current ratio has been below 1.0x every year of the window and fell to 0.68x in FY2026, a persistent negative working capital position typical of the business model rather than a new stress [F180][F171][F172].
Payout exceeded free cash flow in FY2025 and FY2026, at 116.6% and 100.7%, leaving little room if free cash flow dips again as it did in FY2025 [D402][D453][D412].
Capex at 1.40x D&A is the window high, so free cash flow now depends on that spending converting into growth [D446][D395].
Operating margin: a FY2027 reading back above the 24.3% FY2025 high would confirm the FY2026 dip was mix-driven, while a move below the 22.1% median would extend the compression [D647][D648].
Free cash flow to net income: a recovery above the 1.02x window median would restore cover for the payout, which was 100.7% of free cash flow in FY2026 [D660][D453].
Capex against revenue: a FY2027 ratio below the 5.1% FY2026 level would ease the capital-intensity drag on free cash flow [D440].
